{{Quote|Translated from the Kaminoan by Ryan Kaufman|Opening line of "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="Tale" />}}
"'''The Tale of the Aiwha Pod'''" was a [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] tale [[Translator/Legends|translated]] into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] from the [[Kaminoan (language)/Legends|Kaminoan language]] by [[Ryan Kaufman]]. It was a story on why the [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwha]] [[Species/Legends|species]] ruled the [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and were respected by all creatures of the world.

The protagonist of the story was a [[Deity/Legends|god]]-beast named [[Protas]], considered to be both the most powerful beast and ruler of the oceans. His claim for rule was challenged first by a titan of the deep, [[Melkorr]], then by the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] and legion [[kikla]]. He defeated both sets of challengers and became arrogant in his old age. In such a mind-set, he prevented a [[Unidentified aiwha pod|pod]] of aiwha from fleeing [[Winter/Legends|winter]], requesting they return to the increasingly [[Temperature/Legends|cold]] northern [[Water/Legends|waters]]. The creatures realized they would [[Death/Legends|die]] if they complied with the unreasonable request and fought Protas, defeating the god-beast only when [[Unidentified aiwha|one]] of their own sacrificed himself.

==Description==
{{Quote|And that is why, to this day, the aiwha rule the oceans and are accorded a measure of respect even among the largest, most powerful, and most plentiful beasts.|Ryan Kaufman, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="Tale" />}}
"The Tale of the Aiwha Pod" was a mythical tale originating from the [[Water/Legends|aquatic]]<ref name="Tale" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="Kamino">{{Film|II}}</ref> It served as a lesson to the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] on why the non-sentient [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwha]] [[Species/Legends|species]] were to be afforded respect and seen as the rulers of the vast [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] of the planet. The story was originally told in the [[Kaminoan (language)/Legends|Kaminoan language]], and [[Ryan Kaufman]] [[Translator/Legends|translated]] the tale onto a single page [[Writing/Legends|written]] in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]].<ref name="Tale" />

==Synopsis==
===Challenged for supremacy===
{{Quote|Protas, meet me in battle, and we shall decide who is the ruler of this blue kingdom.|Melkorr, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="Tale" />}}
[[File:Kamino.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Kamino, origin of "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"]]
The story commenced in the distant past, before the dawn of the second [[Star/Legends|sun]] when the oceans of Kamino were ruled by a [[Magic/Legends|mystical]] being named [[Protas]]. [[Melkorr]], a massive titan from the deep, challenged Protas' claim as the most powerful in the seas and met Protas on the underwater ridge of [[Thalina]], where Melkorr attacked the [[Deity/Legends|god]]-beast with a jaw full of sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] and large, pointed fins. Melkorr attempted to use his size and power to overwhelm Protas, with the two [[Battle of Thalina|battling]] for six [[Standard day/Legends|days]] and nights. Protas used his agility and speed to evade the titan's attacks and eventually drove Melkorr to exhaustion. The god-beast then took advantage of Melkorr's faltering and dealt a [[Death/Legends|killing]] blow, which left the seas [[Blood/Legends|bloodied]] and the [[Fish/Legends|fish]] [[Foodstuff/Legends|fed]] for an [[Time/Legends|eon]].<ref name="Tale" />

An [[Army/Legends|army]] of sentient [[kikla]], with the belief that their large numbers would make up for their comparatively small size and allow them to overwhelm Protas, made the next challenge. Protas met them in the deep waters of the [[Ancient Trench]], where they [[Battle of the Ancient Trench|fought]] for a [[Standard month/Legends|month]]. Although numerous, the kikla were divided in [[Brain/Legends|mind]], arguing among themselves. Due to their comparative size, they would also leave only small wounds on the god-beast. In contrast, Protas was of a single mind and slowly ate the kikla to maintain strength. At the new [[Moon/Legends|moon]], Protas was again victorious when the last kikla was consumed.<ref name="Tale" />

===The arrogance and fall of Protas===
{{Quote|You cannot pass. Go back to the north seas and freeze.''"<br />"''Why, Master Protas?''"<br />"''Because it pleases me.|Protas and the aiwha pod, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="Tale" />}}
[[File:Aiwhas-ARCT.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Aiwha, respected by all life on Kamino]]
The victories over Melkorr and the kikla gave Protas confirmation of his power, and in his advanced age, he became arrogant. He eventually came across a [[Unidentified aiwha pod|pod]] of aiwha who were swimming south to avoid the [[Temperature/Legends|cold]] [[Winter/Legends|winter]]. For amusement, Protas refused to let them continue, blocking their path and instructing the aiwha to return north. With the knowledge that they would die if they turned back, the aiwha [[Destruction of Protas|attacked]] without warning or desire for fame or glory. Despite the combined swarming tactics of the kikla and the powerful attacks of Melkorr, the aiwha still could not deal a killing blow through Protas' thick skin.<ref name="Tale" />

One [[Unidentified aiwha|aiwha]] noticed Protas momentarily expose the soft flesh of his throat and clamped onto it in a sacrificial attempt to defeat him. Realizing the danger, Protas attempted to dislodge the aiwha by smashing it with his fins, but it would not let go, even in death. His sacrifice allowed the rest of the pod to deal a final blow and end the god-beast's life. Their defeating Protas brought peace to the seas and was the reason why aiwha were given respect by all the creatures of Kamino, great and small.<ref name="Tale" />

==Behind the scenes==
"The Tale of the Aiwha Pod" was featured in a [[The Tale of the Aiwha Pod (short story)|short story]] of the same name, which was written by [[Ryan Kaufman (real person)|Ryan Kaufman]] and published by [[Prima Games]] in their [[2005]] [[Star Wars: Republic Commando: Prima Official Game Guide|game guide]] for the ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]]. The story was written with an [[in-universe]] perspective and attributed as "Translated from the Kaminoan by Ryan Kaufman," thus making the real-world author an in-universe character.<ref name="Tale" />
